title: keryx as an ACP client: drive external ACP agents with keryx context and policy

AC1.note: src/harness/external/acp-client.process.test.ts:207 describe("AC1 — a full ACP turn over a real pipe") — tests at 208 and 250 drive the fake agent over ExternalSpawnPort real pipes through initialize/session-new/session-prompt to stopReason end_turn (cwd absolute, folded ExternalEvents, status Completed) and the unsupported-protocolVersion case ending Error with a named reason and a killed child.

AC2.note: src/harness/external/acp-permission.test.ts:50 (kind→risk→gate table), :97 "the clamp is recorded: trust and auto are lowered, ask is not" (clampForeignMode trust/auto→ask, ask stays ask), :103 "UNCLAMPED, trust would have auto-approved an execute — the clamp is what stops it"; :110 describe("the answer: allow_once only, never allow_always"). Wire-level confirmation in src/harness/external/acp-client.process.test.ts:283 describe("AC2 — the permission bridge on the wire").

AC3.note: src/harness/external/acp-permission.test.ts:137 describe("AC3 — fail closed") — unattended/no-TTY/no-approver, timeout and human-no all answered reject_once (or cancelled), one decision entry per request with risk, gate decision, verdict, timedOut and reason. Process-level: src/harness/external/acp-client.process.test.ts:319 describe("AC3 — an unattended run fails closed"), tests at 320 and 359 show the fake agent received the rejection and the tool was not reported as run.

AC4.note: src/harness/external/acp-client.process.test.ts:386 describe("AC4 — keryx advertises only what it serves"), tests at 387 and 411: read-only run advertises fs.readTextFile true / fs.writeTextFile false / terminal false / no elicitation; --write additionally advertises fs.writeTextFile true; terminal never advertised. fs/write_text_file in read-only, terminal/create and elicitation/create in every run each get a named JSON-RPC error and are recorded; no file created, no process spawned.

AC5.note: src/harness/external/acp-client.process.test.ts:434 describe("AC5 — fs requests run only inside keryx's confined code"), test at 435: symlinked-parent escape, ../ traversal, agent credential files and managed flow files all refused; approved write goes through the AC2 bridge as risk write; project tree hash byte-identical before/after; --write diff saved as patch artifact and never applied (line 483-489). Test at 494: --write run with nobody to ask writes nothing. Ancestor-resolution fix covered by confineToRoot changes noted in journal T13 (2026-09-23T01:04:35Z).

AC6.note: src/harness/external/acp-client.process.test.ts:515 describe("AC6 — context through keryx's own MCP server"), test at 516: session/new carries one stdio mcpServers entry launching process.execPath + src/cli.ts serve-mcp --read-only --cwd <project> (not 'keryx' from PATH). Test at 538: MCP module unavailable → run proceeds, records context: not-offered with reason 'MCP module is disabled'. Test at 551: buildExternalPrompt's first prompt; resource blocks only sent when agent advertised promptCapabilities.embeddedContext. supply-mcp.test.ts covers serve-mcp --read-only listing no tool marked mutating: true (shared with runtime.ts guard).

AC7.note: src/harness/external/acp-client.process.test.ts:602 describe("AC7 — every run is a keryx session"), test at 603: keryx sessions lists provider acp:gemini-acp; persisted record holds redacted assistant text (token redaction verified at 613/641-643), fs requests with outcomes, argv, worktreePath, agentInfo name/version, usage, and raw never-converted cost; mode requested/effective/clamped recorded. Test at 648: a cost the agent never reported is recorded as 'missing', never 0 (outcome.acp?.cost toBe('missing')).

AC8.note: Addendum: no real Gemini CLI run happened in this verification (gemini not installed in this environment); AC8 is about the command surface and routing, verified end-to-end with the fake ACP agent fixture (acp-client.process.test.ts) and keryx acp --fixture interop (acp-interop.process.test.ts), not a live gemini-acp binary.

AC9.note: src/harness/external/acp-interop.process.test.ts:83 describe(AC9 - keryx answers keryx's own permission question). keryx-as-client drives keryx-as-agent via keryx acp --fixture <script> end to end; a gated tool in the inner keryx sends a real session/request_permission to the outer keryx; outer keryx answers by its own policy (denied when unattended, allowed after an injected approval); the inner turn's record shows that outcome. No real gemini/claude CLI involved - this is keryx-to-keryx over the ACP wire, interop only.

AC10.note: src/harness/external/acp-client.process.test.ts:714 describe(AC10 - the honest limit: the agent's own tools never reach keryx), test at 715: fake agent writes a file with its own filesystem calls (writeOwnFile step) instead of ACP; the file lands only in the disposable worktree, which is removed afterwards, is not recorded as a keryx-mediated write, and the project tree is unchanged. Docs (docs/docs/guides/acp-client.md) state the limits: unadvertised capabilities are requests not boundaries, classification relies on the agent's own tool-call description, calls to keryx's own MCP servers bypass the permission bridge, the agent process is not OS-sandboxed in this flow, and the disposable worktree is the load-bearing containment (D-08).

AC11.note: docs/docs/guides/acp-client.md is the ACP client page: usage, permission mapping table, advertised capabilities, record format and AC10 limits. README.md:258,295,309 links it. docs/requirements/keryx-external-agent-runtime/README.md:23-48 notes the third (acp) transport and worktree-write support. keryx agents external list shows gemini-acp with transport acp (src/harness/external/registry.ts:69,83; registry.test.ts:23). No real Gemini CLI run happened in this verification (gemini not installed in this environment) - AC11 is about the command surface and docs, verified with the fake agent fixture and keryx acp --fixture interop, not a live gemini-acp binary.

AC12.note: Correction: gemini is not on PATH here, but 'claude' IS on PATH in this environment (it resolves to the Claude Code CLI itself at ~/.nvm/.../bin/claude, not a dedicated agent binary) - flagging this so the record is accurate rather than asserting both are absent. This does not weaken AC12: the ACP client test suite (acp-client.process.test.ts, acp-interop.process.test.ts, acp-permission.test.ts, acp-fs.test.ts) never spawns the registry's claude-cli or gemini-acp binaries - it drives a repo fixture fake-agent script (FAKE_AGENT) over real stdio pipes, or keryx's own --fixture ACP mode, so the tests are independent of whatever CLIs happen to be on PATH and make no network calls.
